correctness.rationale: For each of r internally disjoint paths, divergence-zero forces a constant branch flow; pole balance gives one linear condition. The constrained orthogonal projection is explicitly Qx_i=mean_i-(sum of all means)/(length_i*S). All signs of Q and P=I-Q entries follow from length_i*S>1. Absolute row sums yield B_i=1+(r-2)/(length_i*S) and A_i=2-2/length_i+((r-2)*length_i+2)/(length_i^2*S). The latter is strictly convex in the reciprocal length; the shortest-minus-longest difference factors as (u-v)((r-2)-2*sum of interior reciprocal lengths)/S, nonnegative because simple graphs have at most one length-one path. This proves the all-parameter shortest-arm extremum and exact formulas, with sign-pattern sharpness. The strict global bounds follow from S>1/s and are approached by (s,M,...,M) with M tending to infinity. The standalone package checker independently reconstructs anchored incidence matrices: 64 exact rational cases, 150 numerical cases, 1,064 equal-arm identities, 84 large-contrast bounds; these tests do not replace proof.

value.rationale: The sharp operator norms quantify the worst uniform output-edge perturbation of a natural ℓ2 graph least-squares gradient extraction, which Hilbert norm one cannot predict. Every simple generalized-theta network receives an exact all-size answer and a rigorous shortest-path location of worst sensitivity. The contrast family produces nearly r-fold amplification despite each input edge bounded by one; equal-length arms stay bounded below three. This is a natural complete graph-family stability classification with a concrete high-degree, long-bypass design effect, not just an arbitrary parameter experiment.
